sentences.en: And at that point, half the crowd goes berserk and invades the pitch, starting fires, demolishing bits of the stadium and stuff.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，一半的人群陷入疯狂，冲进球场，开始纵火，拆毁体育场的部分设施等等。

sentences.en: And eventually, riot police have to clear the stadium.
sentences.zh: 最终，防暴警察不得不清场。

sentences.en: Now, needless to say, they don't get to play that second game.
sentences.zh: 不用说，他们没能打成第二场比赛。

sentences.en: They forfeit the second game.
sentences.zh: 他们弃权了第二场比赛。

sentences.en: Not that they were going to win it anyway.
sentences.zh: 反正他们也不可能赢。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Obviously, that's not why disco fell from grace.
sentences.zh: 显然，那并不是迪斯科失宠的原因。

sentences.en: But that moment.
sentences.zh: 但那一刻。

sentences.en: No, it's a symptom, not a cause.
sentences.zh: 不，那只是症状，不是原因。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That becomes the symbolic moment when disco falls to grace.
sentences.zh: 那成为了迪斯科失宠的象征性时刻。

sentences.en: Because actually, that's the middle of 1979.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上，那是1979年年中。

sentences.en: By the autumn of 1979, disco has totally vanished from the US singles chart.
sentences.zh: 到了1979年秋天，迪斯科已经彻底从美国单曲榜上消失了。

sentences.en: What's interesting about that, and a bit odd, is that it is from Chicago that house music will emerge.
sentences.zh: 有趣且有点奇怪的是，浩室音乐（House music）正是从芝加哥兴起的。

sentences.en: And house music will underpin the revival of dance culture and clubbing in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 而浩室音乐将支撑起90年代舞蹈文化和夜店文化的复兴。

sentences.en: Now, this will amaze our listeners, or some of them.
sentences.zh: 这会让我们的听众，或者其中一些人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: But you are the Michael Gove of history, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 但你就是历史界的迈克尔·戈夫（Michael Gove），不是吗？

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Because Michael Gove, the British cabinet minister, is famous for his love of dancing.
sentences.zh: 因为英国内阁大臣迈克尔·戈夫以热爱跳舞而闻名。

sentences.en: And he will go to Aberdeen or something in his suit and go clubbing on his own.
sentences.zh: 他会穿着西装去阿伯丁之类的地方，独自去夜店跳舞。

sentences.en: And you too are a great lover of house music, are you not?
sentences.zh: 而你也是浩室音乐的忠实爱好者，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, I was.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我曾经是。

sentences.en: Not now.
sentences.zh: 现在不是了。

sentences.en: I remember about three weeks after Katie was born, my oldest daughter.
sentences.zh: 我记得在我大女儿凯蒂出生大约三周后。

sentences.en: And I went, and I just had a brilliant time.
sentences.zh: 我去了，玩得非常开心。

sentences.en: And then I thought, this is so undignified.
sentences.zh: 然后我想，这太不庄重了。

sentences.en: From this point on, I'm going to behave as I should according to my age.
sentences.zh: 从现在起，我要表现得符合我的年龄。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 噢，真的吗？

sentences.en: And that is a vow I have always stuck to.
sentences.zh: 这是我一直遵守的誓言。

sentences.en: Oh, my word.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's an incentive for people.
sentences.zh: 所以这对人们来说是个激励。

sentences.en: If you become an Athelstan, the rest is history, so our elite members, maybe you can persuade Tom to hold one of our Athelstan get-togethers in a nightclub.
sentences.zh: 如果你成为了Athelstan会员，剩下的就是历史了，所以我们的精英成员们，也许你们可以说服汤姆在夜店举办一次我们的Athelstan聚会。

sentences.en: Well, so there was a club in Brixton called The Fridge.
sentences.zh: 好吧，布里克斯顿曾有一家叫“冰箱”（The Fridge）的夜店。

sentences.en: The Fridge.
sentences.zh: “冰箱”。

sentences.en: And they had that session called Love Muscle.
sentences.zh: 他们有个叫“爱之肌肉”（Love Muscle）的活动。

sentences.en: Love Muscle.
sentences.zh: “爱之肌肉”。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's quite disco, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，很有迪斯科风格，对吧？

sentences.en: Great days.
sentences.zh: 美好的日子。

sentences.en: That's fair.
sentences.zh: 说得对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think what's happened is that at the end of the 1970s, one of the reasons that Disco Foolsome Grace is simply generational turnover.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为发生的事情是，在70年代末，迪斯科失宠的原因之一仅仅是代际更替。

sentences.en: So if you're 20 in 1970, you're Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 如果你在1970年20岁，你就是汤姆·霍兰德。

sentences.en: You're 30 in 1980.
sentences.zh: 你在1980年就30岁了。

sentences.en: And you want to do something a bit more dignified.
sentences.zh: 你想做点更庄重的事情。

sentences.en: You're too old for it.
sentences.zh: 你年纪太大了，不适合那个了。

sentences.en: You know, you've got kids, all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你有孩子了，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: But also, of course, if you're 20 in 1980, you don't want to listen to Granddad's Disco.
sentences.zh: 但当然，如果你在1980年20岁，你也不想听爷爷辈的迪斯科。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: You want something new, don't you?
sentences.zh: 你想要点新鲜的，对吧？

sentences.en: So that's an element of it.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是其中一个因素。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Madonna.
sentences.zh: 麦当娜。

sentences.en: I also think there is a deeper thing, which is that at the end of the 1970s, there is generally a backlash against gay rights and against what's seen as the permissive liberalism.
sentences.zh: 我还认为有一个更深层的原因，那就是在70年代末，人们普遍对同性恋权利和所谓的放纵自由主义产生了抵触。

sentences.en: And there are lots of examples of that.
sentences.zh: 有很多这样的例子。

sentences.en: But also, Dominic, I mean, that is tied in with, of course, the great calamity that hits gay community in the United States and then around the world.
sentences.zh: 但多米尼克，我的意思是，这当然与袭击美国乃至全世界同性恋群体的巨大灾难有关。

sentences.en: AIDS.
sentences.zh: 艾滋病。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: And I think there's a sense in which, so just on the backlash, there have been people, politicians.
sentences.zh: 我认为在某种意义上，就这种抵触情绪而言，确实有一些人，一些政客。

sentences.en: So the most famous one is a woman in Florida called Anita Bryant, who was a singer who had promoted orange juice.
sentences.zh: 最著名的是佛罗里达州一位叫安妮塔·布莱恩特（Anita Bryant）的女性，她是一位曾为橙汁做过广告的歌手。

sentences.en: And she launched a campaign called Save Our Children and gets loads of attention for it in 1977.
sentences.zh: 她在1977年发起了一场名为“拯救我们的孩子”（Save Our Children）的运动，并因此受到了极大的关注。

sentences.en: And there was indeed, there was a referendum called the Briggs Initiative in California a year later.
sentences.zh: 一年后，加利福尼亚州确实进行了一次名为“布里格斯倡议”（Briggs Initiative）的公投。

sentences.en: Again, all the stuff about saving children.
sentences.zh: 同样，都是关于拯救孩子的内容。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of that.
sentences.zh: 所以这方面有很多。

sentences.en: And then there's a lot of stuff about what's seen as the unhealthiness.
sentences.zh: 还有很多关于所谓“不健康”的讨论。

sentences.en: This is including from within the gay community itself.
sentences.zh: 这甚至包括来自同性恋群体内部的声音。

sentences.en: People talking about the unhealthiness of these clubs in New York and stuff, clubs with slightly disconcerting names.
sentences.zh: 人们谈论纽约这些夜店的不健康状况等等，那些夜店的名字听起来有些令人不安。

sentences.en: The Ramrod, the Mindshaft, the Cockring.
sentences.zh: 拉姆罗德、心灵矿井、阴茎环。

sentences.en: But these presumably are more kind of the sex is foregrounded in those clubs rather than the music.
sentences.zh: 但这些夜店大概更多是强调性，而不是音乐。

sentences.en: The Mindshaft.
sentences.zh: 心灵矿井。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: One critic called it one part erotic paradise, one part open wound.
sentences.zh: 一位评论家称它为“一半是情色天堂，一半是开放性伤口”。

sentences.en: And somebody else called it the Mount Rushmore of filth, which you can use your own imagination.
sentences.zh: 另一个人称它为“污秽的拉什莫尔山”，你可以发挥自己的想象力。

sentences.en: So AIDS comes, the first reports of AIDS.
sentences.zh: 所以艾滋病来了，关于艾滋病的第一批报道出现了。

sentences.en: One reason that they're perhaps not taken as seriously as they should have been is because they come in the context of a wider discussion about sexually transmitted diseases,
sentences.zh: 人们之所以没有给予应有的重视，原因之一是它们出现在关于性传播疾病的更广泛讨论的背景下，

sentences.en: about massive surge in hepatitis, gonorrhea, intestinal infections, and so on among gay men.
sentences.zh: 关于男同性恋者中肝炎、淋病、肠道感染等疾病的激增。

sentences.en: And actually, the public health clinics in San Francisco and New York are already at the center of big controversies at the end of the 70s,
sentences.zh: 事实上，旧金山和纽约的公共卫生诊所在70年代末就已经处于巨大争议的中心，

sentences.en: because they are sort of saying, calm down, slow down, there's too much of this.
sentences.zh: 因为他们当时在说，冷静点，慢下来，这东西太多了。

sentences.en: And then other people are saying, oh, that's very homophobic of you.
sentences.zh: 然后其他人就说，噢，你这太恐同了。

sentences.en: You're trying to police our lifestyle and all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你们这是在试图管制我们的生活方式，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So actually, the first reports of people with pneumonia.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，关于肺炎患者的最初报告，

sentences.en: It takes time for them to realize that it's something new.
sentences.zh: 人们花了一段时间才意识到这是一种新事物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So the very first report, it's in a gay paper, the New York native in 1981, reporting rumors that an exotic new disease has hit the gay community in New York.
sentences.zh: 所以第一篇报道出现在1981年的一份同性恋报纸《纽约本地人》上，报道了关于一种奇异的新疾病袭击了纽约同性恋社区的传闻。

sentences.en: The headline is, disease rumors largely unfounded, because there is a sort of an understandable impulse to say, you know, this is just yet another slur.
sentences.zh: 标题是“疾病传闻大多毫无根据”，因为当时有一种可以理解的冲动，认为这不过是又一种诽谤。

sentences.en: This is yet another kind of attempt to put us back in our box and to identify us with unhealthiness, which we don't deserve.
sentences.zh: 这又是试图把我们关回笼子里，把我们和不健康联系起来的企图，我们不该遭受这些。

sentences.en: Anyway, so against that background, I think the sort of what you might call the more innocent hedonism of early 70s disco,
sentences.zh: 总之，在这样的背景下，我认为70年代初迪斯科那种可以称之为更纯粹的享乐主义，

sentences.en: the kind of love saves the day, let's all have a wonderful time, that's kind of lost its luster, I would say, by the end of the 70s and by the early 1980s.
sentences.zh: 那种“爱拯救世界”、让我们一起度过美好时光的氛围，到了70年代末和80年代初，我觉得已经失去了光彩。

sentences.en: And of course, I mean, you mentioned house music, but obviously hip hop.
sentences.zh: 当然，我的意思是，你提到了浩室音乐，但显然还有嘻哈音乐。

sentences.en: Hip hop is also beginning to emerge from places like the Bronx, and it's hip hop that's cool, and disco is beginning to seem.
sentences.zh: 嘻哈音乐也开始从布朗克斯等地兴起，嘻哈才是酷的，而迪斯科开始显得……

sentences.en: Partly because of the Boney M stuff and the village people.
sentences.zh: 部分是因为Boney M和乡村人乐队那些东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是啊，当然。

sentences.en: It's just a bit of a joke.
sentences.zh: 它变得有点像个笑话了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's silly in a way that it hadn't been silly in 1972 or 73.
sentences.zh: 它变得愚蠢了，而在1972年或73年时它并不是这样的。

sentences.en: But that kind of euphoric feeling of hedonism does come back.
sentences.zh: 但那种欣快感的享乐主义确实又回来了。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, you know, it goes in cycles, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是一种循环，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's a constant, isn't it, in musical history?
sentences.zh: 这是音乐史上永恒的主题，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: The desire for escapism, for hedonism, for release.
sentences.zh: 对逃避现实、享乐主义和释放自我的渴望。

sentences.en: The interesting thing is whether that tension between being a very individual narcissistic experience,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，那种作为一种非常个人化、自恋的体验，

sentences.en: you dressing up and dancing just for yourself, or are you doing it to commune with other people?
sentences.zh: 你是为了自己打扮跳舞，还是为了与他人交流而跳舞，这种张力如何平衡？

sentences.en: Tom, when you were going to the house clubs, were you a narcissist or were you communing?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，当你去浩室俱乐部时，你是自恋者还是在与人交流？

sentences.en: No, it's communing with other people, because it's the difference between cocaine and ecstasy, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 不，是在与他人交流，因为这就像可卡因和摇头丸的区别，不是吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm not a massive enthusiast for either.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我并不是这两者的狂热爱好者。

sentences.en: But cocaine is more about narcissism, and ecstasy, famously, is about the communal experience.
sentences.zh: 但可卡因更多是关于自恋，而摇头丸众所周知是关于群体体验的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And so those drugs shape the dance cultures that they generate.
sentences.zh: 所以这些药物塑造了它们所产生的舞蹈文化。

sentences.en: They definitely do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And on that bombshell.
sentences.zh: 带着这个重磅炸弹（结束话题）。

sentences.en: What a bombshell.
sentences.zh: 真是个重磅炸弹。

sentences.en: Thank you, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，多米尼克。

sentences.en: DJ Dominic.
sentences.zh: DJ多米尼克。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.zh: 这是我书中被删减的片段之一，《疯狂如地狱》。

sentences.en: Yeah, and you've left out quite a lot, haven't you?
sentences.zh: 是啊，你删掉了很多内容，不是吗？

sentences.en: I have.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There was a load more stuff about the mineshaft.
sentences.zh: 关于矿井俱乐部还有很多内容。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You plumb the depths.
sentences.zh: 你挖掘得很深。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which people are probably happy to have been spared.
sentences.zh: 人们可能很高兴能幸免于难。

sentences.en: You dig deep, but not on this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 你挖掘得很深，但不是在这个播客里。

sentences.en: But thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 但非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Wonderful to see another chunk of your vanished masterpiece brought to light.
sentences.zh: 很高兴看到你那部消失的杰作的另一部分重见天日。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.zh: 再见，各位。

sentences.zh: 下次见。

sentences.zh: 再见。
